---
title: "Mastermind Hub backend"
description: "Private operations snapshots, gateway authorization, retention, and held Cloudflare publication."
---

## Scope and release hold

P0 is a private read API for the infrastructure gateway. Environments contain both
production and staging per product, supplied by the publisher snapshot. The Worker
never fetches source control, deployment providers, quotas or customer data.
Security-related subjects become **Security fix**; security items expose generic
titles, severity and state without bodies, questions or links. The future mobile
entry belongs in Apps, according to the approved design. No UI, replies, device
enrollment, push, publisher installation or Supabase migration ships here.

Code is public; allowlists, keys and operational data must stay out of source.
Publication remains held. The validation workflow has no deploy job, credentials,
DNS changes or provisioning. Release Desk needs explicit deployment authorization,
an independent security review, exact-commit CI and an approved sanitized publisher
sample before the first publish. The only configured hostname is workers.dev.

## Configuration names

| Placement | Name | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Worker secret | `OPS_HUB_PUBLISHER_PUBLIC_KEY` | Base64 raw 32-byte Ed25519 verification key; never the private key |
| Worker and infrastructure server secret | `OPS_HUB_GATEWAY_SECRET` | Shared HMAC key, 43–256 characters |
| Worker and infrastructure server secret | `OPS_HUB_ALLOWED_USER_IDS` | Comma-separated UUIDs, at most ten; invalid configuration denies everyone |
| Infrastructure server var | `OPS_HUB_WORKER_URL` | HTTPS workers.dev origin without path, credentials, query or fragment |
| Worker binding (configuration) | `HUB` | SQLite-backed `OpsHub` namespace; object name `hub:<userId>` |

No actual allowlist, key or live origin is committed. There is no publisher
private-key or push-secret binding in P0. Place the same allowlist in both
services; removing an identity blocks its routes at the Worker as well.

## Publisher contract

Send POST `/ingest`, Content-Type application/json, with
`x-ops-hub-publisher-user` set to the allowlisted UUID and
`x-ops-hub-signature` set to a standard-base64 Ed25519 signature.
Sign the UTF-8 prefix `ops-hub-publisher-v2\nPOST\n/ingest\n<userId>\n`
followed by the **exact request body bytes**. Use a lowercase UUID.
The strict envelope is `{v:2, seq, sentAt, snapshot?, events:[], decisions?:[], observability?}`;
all timestamps are Unix milliseconds. Every successful envelope advances seq.
A retry with the same sequence gets 409 and never appends duplicate events.
Reconcile an unknown outcome through authenticated status before advancing seq.

Snapshot fields are `enabled?`, `pausedReason?`, `needsYou`, `environments`,
`lanes` and `backlog`. The authoritative schemas are
`apps/ops-hub/src/schema.ts`; unknown fields at any depth reject the entire
envelope. Each event has its own strictly increasing seq across all batches.
The signed sentAt must be within 120 seconds. Events cannot be older than 30 days
or more than 120 seconds in the future. Item edits must advance their version.

Environment rows contain `product`, `environment` (production or staging),
`lastRelease` (timestamp or null), `version`, `shortSha`, `commitSubject`,
`deployState` and `ciState`. State values are queued, running, success,
failed, held or unknown. Product/environment pairs are unique.
Secret-shaped and personal text is withheld; security text is reduced again at
ingest. This defense does not replace the Mac publisher's fail-closed sanitizer
or the required sanitized-sample approval.

## Read and lifecycle contract (v2)

GET `/status`, `/snapshot`, `/events?after=<seq>`, `/needs-you`,
`/environments`, `/decisions?after=&category=`, `/observability?since=&series=` and `/hub/export` require a valid gateway assertion.
The infrastructure gateway exposes these routes plus DELETE `/hub`.
Gateway assertions use `x-ops-hub-user`, last 60 seconds, and bind the user,
HTTP method, path and query. Publisher signatures grant ingest only.
Authentication failures return 404. Responses are private, no-store.

An hourly alarm purges events after 30 days and terminal items 30 days after
answered/withdrawn, while open items remain. Snapshot is replaced on ingest;
its needs-you projection comes from the retained item table. Reads independently
filter expired records. Publisher staleness is computed after 15 minutes on every
status read, and persisted by maintenance. With no new publisher activity,
maintenance purges all content at the 30-day horizon and stops scheduling.

A signed snapshot with `enabled:false` durably pauses ingest and read access
while retaining the content. Every route except authenticated status returns 503,
including ingest and DELETE /hub. Only bounded retention maintenance continues;
it does not update staleness or emit alerts. There is no HTTP resume route in P0:
resumption needs an explicitly authorized operator action against the DO, beyond
this code-only delivery. Explicit erasure must run before disabling or de-allowlisting.
DELETE `/hub` clears snapshot, events, items, decisions and observations and leaves only a disabled
replay tombstone (sequence/counters, no content), preventing a captured signed
ingest from recreating erased content. Erase before removing the user from both
allowlists; a de-allowlisted identity cannot reach its object.

## Cost and test evidence

Limits: 256 KiB streamed ingest, 100 events per envelope, 1,000 retained events,
100 retained items, 100 lanes/backlog entries, 40 environment rows and 120
successful ingests per object per hour. Reads return at most 200 events. Export is paginated by section and row cursor;
each page contains at most 200 rows. There are no outgoing provider requests, queues,
cron triggers, retries or fan-out. Invalid assertions do not touch the DO.
Maintenance uses fixed-size deletion batches. Disabled hubs run only retention
cleanup; explicit erasure and the final retention horizon stop scheduling. Stop reduces background work; it
cannot prevent the billing of an incoming request reaching Cloudflare.

On an admitted host, run from `apps/ops-hub`:

```sh
ttr resources run -- bun run test
ttr resources run -- bun run test:runtime
ttr resources run -- bun run type-check
ttr resources run -- bun run lint
```

The runtime suite starts a finite loopback workerd instance through the existing
cf/Vite harness, with ephemeral fixture keys and isolated SQLite persistence,
then closes it. It tests forged signatures, replay/skew/size/schema rejection,
environment redaction, isolation, persistence/restart, retention and kill/erase
fences. Unit tests exercise real SQLite retention and bounded maintenance work.
These commands do not run a release build or contact hosted services.
Compatibility date is pinned to 2026-10-19, supported by the repository's
pinned workerd. CI owns the separate release-build check.

Persisted per-series row counters make cap checks constant-size;
new rows and retention deletions update counters in the same SQLite transaction.

Logical row counters and deletion batch sizes use SQL RETURNING rows. Cloudflare's
rowsWritten metric also counts index updates and cannot serve as a logical row
count; see the [SQLite storage API](https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/api/sqlite-storage-api/).
The workerd regression checks counter equality after duplicate buckets, a forced
transaction rollback and restart. Billing additionally includes maintained indexes;
logical row/statement caps are bounds on work, not a claim of zero storage cost.

## Frozen publisher contract: schema v2

Version 1 is rejected. The signature domain prefix is ops-hub-publisher-v2.
The top-level fields are exactly v, seq, sentAt, snapshot (optional), events,
decisions (optional; defaults to an empty array) and observability (optional).
All objects reject unknown keys. The envelope is limited to 256 KiB, a snapshot
to 128 KiB and each needs-you item to 4 KiB, measured as UTF-8 JSON bytes.

Decisions accept at most 50 rows per ingest and retain the newest 1,000 rows for
at most 30 days. Each row has id (1–80 ASCII identifier characters), at (Unix ms),
title (120 characters), by (mastermind, user, or role: followed by 1–32 ASCII
letters/digits/spaces/underscores/hyphens), category (auto/delegated/user), area
(security/release/product/infra/org/quota/cost), why (280 characters), risk
(low/med/high), and reversible (boolean). IDs are stable and immutable: conflicting
content for an existing ID rejects the ingest. Repeating the same ID/content is
idempotent. Security-area rows store and return **only id, at, title, area, risk**;
why, by, category and reversible are discarded before storage. Category-filtered
reads therefore exclude security rows; unfiltered reads include them.

GET /decisions accepts optional after and category. The response contains decisions
and nextAfter; use the returned timestamp:ID cursor verbatim to avoid skipping rows
that share a timestamp. The page limit is 200. The initial cursor is 0.

When observability is present, all six arrays below are required. Numeric values
are finite; timestamps are nonnegative safe-integer Unix milliseconds. Identifiers
reject secret-shaped text. Per-field limits:

| Array | Exact row fields and limits | Batch cap | Retention/storage |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| quota_series | instance: 1–64 ASCII identifier chars; t; pct: 0–100 | 100 | 7 days, 80,672 total rows, at most 16 instances |
| speed_series | model: 1–80 ASCII model identifier chars; t; tok_s_p50: 0–1,000,000 | 100 | 30 days, newest 10,000 rows, at most 16 models |
| children_series | t; provider: 1–32 ASCII identifier chars; model: 1–80 chars; running/started/finished: integers 0–1,000,000 | 100 | 30 days, newest 10,000 rows, at most 16 provider/model pairs |
| staff | role: 1–64 ASCII identifier chars; title: 120 chars; state; last_active; model: 1–80 chars; runs_today: integer 0–1,000,000 | 100 unique roles | Snapshot, replaced on every supplied observability batch |
| ci | repo: owner/name, at most 100 ASCII chars; t; queued/running: integers 0–1,000,000 | 100 | 30 days, newest 10,000 rows, at most 16 repos |
| cadence | product: 1–64 ASCII identifier chars; last_prod_at: Unix ms or null | 40 unique products | Snapshot, replaced with staff |

Staff states are idle, queued, running, waiting, success, failed, held, paused,
stopped and unknown. Model identifiers may additionally contain slash and colon;
repo names contain one slash. Rows beyond a table cap evict the oldest rows.
Quota timestamps are floored to two-minute buckets; the last value for an
instance/bucket replaces the earlier value. Other series upsert by dimension/t.
Children dimensions include both provider and model. Points older than their
retention window or more than 120 seconds in the future reject the ingest.

GET /observability accepts since (Unix ms, default 0) and series (one of the six
array names, default quota_series). It returns series, points and pointCap=500;
time-series responses also include bucketMs. Reads select the last actual point
in each time bucket, fairly dividing the cap across up to 16 dimensions. A bounded
dimension registry avoids full-history dimension scans; primary-key range lookups
select each bucket endpoint without scanning every raw point. Staff
and cadence return their current snapshot. Historical rows are filtered by their
retention window before downsampling. This endpoint never fetches providers.

The normal hourly alarm is armed before committing accepted content and retained across heartbeats. Each maintenance pass
purges at most eight batches of 512 rows per time series, plus bounded events,
items and decisions. An expired-row backlog schedules a one-minute catch-up pass;
persisted deletion progress survives retry/restart. Row caps bound the remaining
work, and no pass starts an unbounded loop. After 30 days without ingest, all
content, including stale snapshots and open items, is purged and scheduling ends.
Disabled state returns 503 for every non-status route and retains data. Only
retention-purge work continues, without staleness updates; it stops after the
final 30-day horizon. DELETE /hub is a separate explicit purge that clears content,
sets a durable erasure tombstone and cancels the alarm. A late erased-object alarm
exits without scheduling more work.

GET /hub/export uses section (snapshot/events/needs_you/decisions/metrics/
observability_snapshot), after (row cursor, default 0), and optional seq. Each
response includes v=2, seq, section, rows, nextAfter and the section list. Traverse
each section until nextAfter is null, passing the first page's seq throughout;
409 means the hub changed and export must restart. Every page is bounded to 200
rows and filters expired content. This keeps the full export usable with the
same two-MiB gateway response ceiling even at the quota storage cap.
